title: How many cubes have three digits, and can a cube end in two zeros?
description: The cubes are followed from four cubed to ten cubed to count those with exactly three digits. Then the zeros at the end of ten cubed show how zeros come in a cube. Keeko doubts the zeros, because one hundred seems to be a cube.
teaching_notes: One idea: find where the digit count changes, and see that each zero at the end of a number gives three zeros in its cube. Watch for students who think any number ending in zeros is a cube.

source: How many cubes have exactly 3 digits, and can a cube end in
video_script.why: The child counts cubes by digits by finding where the digit count changes, and tests whether zeros can end a cube.
video_script.substitution: Cube the whole numbers one by one until the digit count changes, and cube ten to see how many zeros come.
video_script.anchor: a row of cube cards from one cubed up, each showing its number of digits
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees two zeros at the end of one hundred and says it is a cube. One hundred is ten times ten, only two tens, and a cube needs three tens.
video_script.payoff_line: There are five three digit cubes, and no cube ends in exactly two zeros

final_answer.value: Five 3 digit cubes; no cube ends in exactly two zeros
final_answer.spoken: there are five three digit cubes, and no cube ends in exactly two zeros

hold_back: no cube ends in exactly two zeros
maths_rules: the 3 digit cubes are 5³ to 9³: 125, 216, 343, 512, 729, five cubes
10³ = 1000 ends in three zeros; each zero at the end of a number gives three zeros at the end of its cube, so exactly two is impossible
video_script.design: One idea: the digit count changes at known cubes, and zeros come in threes. Wrong idea: two zeros at the end make a cube. The cube cards are in the anchor band and the working lines sit below.

<bookmark mark='row'/>It is about cubes, which are numbers made by multiplying a number by itself three times.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many cubes have exactly three digits, and can a cube end in exactly two zeros?

<bookmark mark='change'/>To count the cubes with three digits, we find where the digit count changes.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many cubes have exactly 3 digits; can a cube end in exactly two zeros?

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to count the cubes with three digits, and decide about two zeros.

beats.on_screen: where 3 digits begin: 4³ = 64 has 2 digits; 5³ = 125 has 3 digits
narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step one, find where three digits begin.
Four cubed is sixty four, which has two digits.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five cubed is one hundred twenty five, which has three digits.

beats.on_screen: where 3 digits end: 9³ = 729 has 3 digits; 10³ = 1000 has 4 digits; the 3 digit cubes are 5³ to 9³ = 125, 216, 343, 512, 729

marks.list: the five cubes from 5³ to 9³ are listed and counted

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, find where three digits end.
Nine cubed is seven hundred twenty nine, which still has three digits.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten cubed is one thousand, which has four digits.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The cubes with three digits are five cubed to nine cubed, which are five cubes.

beats.on_screen: 10³ = 1000 ends in three zeros; each zero at the end of a number gives 3 zeros at the end of its cube: 3, 6, 9 zeros, never 2

marks.ten: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 is written, with its three zeros circled
marks.rule: each zero at the end of a number gives three zeros in its cube
marks.never: the counts 3, 6, 9 are listed and 2 is left out

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step three, look at the zeros.
Ten times ten times ten is one thousand, which ends in three zeros.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Each zero at the end of a number gives three zeros at the end of its cube.
<bookmark mark='never'/>The zeros come in threes, so exactly two cannot happen.

beats.on_screen: Answer: five 3 digit cubes; no cube ends in exactly two zeros

marks.ans: five 3 digit cubes; no cube ends in exactly two zeros is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>There are five three digit cubes, and no cube ends in exactly two zeros.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says 100 is a cube; 10 × 10 = 100 shows two tens, then a third 10 is added to make 1000 and the bubble is struck through

marks.tens: 10 × 10 = 100 is written with two tens circled
marks.fix: a third 10 joins to make 1000 and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one hundred is a cube, because it ends in two zeros.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>But ten times ten is one hundred, and that uses only two tens.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A cube needs three tens, and that gives one thousand.
